why: D9, the one place Kotlin is genuinely harder than Java. Java is in `scope.NOT_APPLICABLE` because the JLS gives variables and methods separate namespaces, so a local can never shadow a method call. Kotlin has one namespace and an `invoke` convention: `val helper = ::other` then `helper()` calls **other**, not the member `helper()`. A front-end that resolved that bare call to the sibling method would fabricate an edge that reads perfectly plausibly. So the extractor emits nothing for it, and the `_Kotlin` walker in `scope.py` is the independent oracle that confirms the skip really happened. `audit()` is the control in the same body: not shadowed, so it must still resolve.

refusals.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `val helper = ::other` binds a local for the rest of `go`'s body, so `helper()` invokes the local through Kotlin's `invoke` convention — not the sibling method of the same name. Resolving it to `Runner.helper` is the exact fabrication D9 exists to catch, and it is the plausible-looking one a Java-trained reader would accept.

excluded: `helper()` is labelled as reaching nothing at all. It does not reach `Runner.helper` (shadowed by the local, see false_positives) and it does not reach `Runner.other` either — that would mean resolving the `::other` reference stored in the local, which is inference. Both omissions are the decision, so neither is labelled as an edge to miss.
